scope: Genesis 37–41, all 169 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Genesis 37–41.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Renders the paired settle/sojourn language naturally while retaining Canaan.
verses.before: Jacob settled in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Canaan.
verses.after: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father had lived as a resident foreigner.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob settled in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Keeps Joseph’s age, work, maternal group, and ambiguous bad report without deciding whether it was true.
verses.before: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers; he was a youth with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. And Joseph brought a bad report about them to their father.
verses.after: This is the family account of Jacob. Joseph was seventeen years old and tended the flock with his brothers. He worked as a young helper with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives, and he brought their father a bad report about them.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers; he was a youth with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. And Joseph brought a bad report about them to their father.

verses.rationale: Preserves paternal favoritism and chooses a defensible garment rendering without importing the uncertain many-colors tradition.
verses.before: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the son of his old age. And he made him a long robe.
verses.after: Now Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons because Joseph was the son of his old age, and he made him a special long robe.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the son of his old age. And he made him a long robe.

verses.rationale: Carries the Hebrew peace language into idiomatic English and makes the comparison explicit.
verses.before: But when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.
verses.after: When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a peaceful word to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.

verses.rationale: Uses direct narrative syntax while preserving the escalation.
verses.before: Now Joseph dreamed a dream, and when he told it to his brothers they hated him even more.
verses.after: Then Joseph had a dream. When he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Joseph dreamed a dream, and when he told it to his brothers they hated him even more.

verses.rationale: Naturalizes the cognate construction dreamed a dream without losing emphasis.
verses.before: He said to them, “Hear this dream that I have dreamed:
verses.after: He said to them, “Listen to this dream I had.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Hear this dream that I have dreamed:

verses.rationale: Keeps all three behold-like surprises and the spatial action in fluent form.
verses.before: Look, we were binding sheaves in the field, and look, my sheaf arose and stood upright; and look, your sheaves gathered around it and bowed down to my sheaf.”
verses.after: We were binding sheaves in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright. Then your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and stood upright; and behold, your sheaves gathered around it and bowed down to my sheaf.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both emphatic challenges and the distinction between dreams and words.
verses.before: His brothers said to him, “Are you indeed to reign over us? Or are you indeed to rule us?” So they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words.
verses.after: His brothers said, “Do you really intend to reign over us? Will you actually rule us?” So they hated him even more because of his dreams and what he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: His brothers said to him, “Are you indeed to reign over us? Or are you indeed to rule us?” So they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated telling and full celestial imagery.
verses.before: Then he dreamed another dream and told it to his brothers and said, “Look, I have dreamed another dream: look, the sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
verses.after: He had another dream and told his brothers: “Listen, I have had another dream. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he dreamed another dream and told it to his brothers and said, “Behold, I have dreamed another dream: behold, the sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Jacob’s own mother interpretation despite the narrative tension after Rachel’s death.
verses.before: But when he told it to his father and to his brothers, his father rebuked him and said, “What is this dream that you have dreamed? Will I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow ourselves to the ground before you?”
verses.after: When he told his father and brothers, his father rebuked him: “What kind of dream is this? Are your mother, your brothers, and I really going to come and bow to the ground before you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when he told it to his father and to his brothers, his father rebuked him and said, “What is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow ourselves to the ground before you?”

verses.rationale: Expresses the idiom of guarding the matter as continuing attention.
verses.before: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter.
verses.after: His brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter in mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter.

verses.rationale: Existing wording is clear, concise, and closely reflects the source.
verses.before: Now his brothers went to pasture their father’s flock near Shechem.
verses.after: Now his brothers went to pasture their father’s flock near Shechem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now his brothers went to pasture their father’s flock near Shechem.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the conversational question and renders here I am as readiness.
verses.before: Israel said to Joseph, “Are not your brothers pasturing the flock at Shechem? Come, I will send you to them.” And he said to him, “Here I am.”
verses.after: Israel said to Joseph, “Your brothers are pasturing the flock near Shechem, aren’t they? Come, I want to send you to them.” Joseph answered, “I’m ready.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Israel said to Joseph, “Are not your brothers pasturing the flock at Shechem? Come, I will send you to them.” And he said to him, “Here I am.”

verses.rationale: Uses natural speech while retaining brothers’ and flock’s welfare and the route.
verses.before: So he said to him, “Go now, see if it is well with your brothers and with the flock, and bring me word.” So he sent him from the Valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
verses.after: “Go and see how your brothers and the flock are doing,” Israel said, “and bring word back to me.” So he sent Joseph from the Valley of Hebron, and Joseph came to Shechem.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he said to him, “Go now, see if it is well with your brothers and with the flock, and bring me word.” So he sent him from the Valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unnamed man and field setting in direct English.
verses.before: And a man found him wandering in the field, and the man asked him, “What are you seeking?”
verses.after: A man found him wandering in the fields and asked, “What are you looking for?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a man found him wandering in the field, and the man asked him, “What are you seeking?”

verses.rationale: Naturalizes the exchange while retaining Joseph’s polite request.
verses.before: “I am seeking my brothers,” he said. “Tell me, please, where they are pasturing the flock.”
verses.after: “I’m looking for my brothers,” Joseph answered. “Please tell me where they are tending the flock.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I am seeking my brothers,” he said. “Tell me, please, where they are pasturing the flock.”

verses.rationale: Makes the departure and pursuit explicit without adding motive.
verses.before: And the man said, “They have gone away, for I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’” So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
verses.after: “They have moved on,” the man said. “I heard them say, ‘Let’s go to Dothan.’” Joseph followed his brothers and found them near Dothan.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the man said, “They have gone away, for I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’” So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.

verses.rationale: Preserves conspiracy and its timing in compact narrative prose.
verses.before: They saw him from afar, and before he came near to them they conspired against him to kill him.
verses.after: They saw him in the distance, and before he reached them they plotted together to kill him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They saw him from afar, and before he came near to them they conspired against him to kill him.

verses.rationale: Renders the contemptuous Hebrew literally as master/owner of dreams rather than merely dreamer.
verses.before: They said to one another, “Here comes this dreamer.
verses.after: They said to one another, “Look—here comes the master of dreams!
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to one another, “Here comes this dreamer.

verses.rationale: Keeps murder, concealment, fabricated explanation, and taunting conclusion.
verses.before: Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. Then we will say that a fierce animal has devoured him, and we will see what will become of his dreams.”
verses.after: Come on, let’s kill him and throw him into one of these pits. We can say that a wild animal devoured him. Then we’ll see what becomes of his dreams.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. Then we will say that a fierce animal has devoured him, and we will see what will become of his dreams.”

verses.rationale: Shows that Reuben stopped the immediate murder while his fuller plan to return Joseph still lay ahead.
verses.before: But when Reuben heard it, he rescued him out of their hands, saying, “Let us not take his life.”
verses.after: When Reuben heard this, he intervened to rescue Joseph from their hands. “We must not take his life,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Reuben heard it, he rescued him out of their hands, saying, “Let us not take his life.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the blood/hand repetitions and discloses Reuben’s plan.
verses.before: Reuben said to them, “Shed no blood; throw him into this pit here in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him”—that he might rescue him out of their hand and restore him to his father.
verses.after: “Do not shed blood,” Reuben told them. “Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him.” Reuben intended to rescue him from their hands and return him to his father.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Reuben said to them, “Shed no blood; throw him into this pit here in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him”—that he might rescue him out of their hand and restore him to his father.

verses.rationale: Keeps the forceful stripping and repeats the garment description.
verses.before: So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe, the long robe that was on him.
verses.after: When Joseph reached his brothers, they stripped off his robe—the special long robe he was wearing—
verses.tsw_comparator: So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe, the long robe that was on him.

verses.rationale: Retains the stark repeated pit and explicit lack of water.
verses.before: And they took him and threw him into a pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it.
verses.after: and they took him and threw him into the pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they took him and threw him into a pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the moral juxtaposition, cargo list, origin, and destination.
verses.before: Then they sat down to eat. And looking up they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing gum, balm, and resin, on their way to carry it down to Egypt.
verses.after: Then they sat down to eat. Looking up, they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying gum, balm, and resin down to Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they sat down to eat. And looking up they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing gum, balm, and resin, on their way to carry it down to Egypt.

verses.rationale: Uses gain for profit while keeping kinship and concealed blood.
verses.before: Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
verses.after: Judah said to his brothers, “What do we gain by killing our brother and covering up his blood?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

verses.rationale: Preserves Judah’s economic proposal and repeated family claim without softening the sale.
verses.before: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be upon him, for he is our brother, our own flesh.” And his brothers listened to him.
verses.after: Come, let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites instead of laying a hand on him. After all, he is our brother, our own flesh.” His brothers agreed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be upon him, for he is our brother, our own flesh.” And his brothers listened to him.

verses.rationale: Uses passives to preserve the Hebrew pronoun ambiguity about who extracted and sold Joseph while retaining both people names.
verses.before: Then Midianite traders passed by. And they drew Joseph up and lifted him out of the pit and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they took Joseph to Egypt.
verses.after: When Midianite merchants passed by, Joseph was pulled and lifted out of the pit, and he was sold to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. They took Joseph to Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Midianite traders passed by. And they drew Joseph up and lifted him out of the pit and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they took Joseph to Egypt.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the location while retaining the grief gesture.
verses.before: When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not in the pit, he tore his clothes
verses.after: When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not in the pit, he tore his clothes

verses.rationale: Preserves Reuben’s broken, self-implicating question rather than resolving it.
verses.before: and returned to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone, and I—where will I go?”
verses.after: He went back to his brothers and cried, “The boy is gone! And I—where can I go now?”
verses.tsw_comparator: and returned to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone, and I—where shall I go?”

verses.rationale: Makes the animal’s age explicit and keeps the garment/blood deception.
verses.before: Then they took Joseph’s robe and slaughtered a goat and dipped the robe in the blood.
verses.after: They took Joseph’s robe, slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they took Joseph’s robe and slaughtered a goat and dipped the robe in the blood.

verses.rationale: Retains the recognition command that echoes in Tamar’s later confrontation and avoids saying the brothers personally delivered it.
verses.before: And they sent the long robe and brought it to their father and said, “This we have found; please examine whether it is your son’s robe or not.”
verses.after: They had the special robe taken to their father with the message, “We found this. Please recognize whether it is your son’s robe or not.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they sent the long robe and brought it to their father and said, “This we have found; please examine whether it is your son’s robe or not.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Jacob’s inference and emphatic cognate wording.
verses.before: And he recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe. A fierce animal has devoured him. Joseph is without doubt torn to pieces.”
verses.after: He recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe! A wild animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe. A fierce animal has devoured him. Joseph is without doubt torn to pieces.”

verses.rationale: Uses familiar mourning language while keeping every action.
verses.before: Then Jacob tore his garments and put sackcloth on his loins and mourned for his son many days.
verses.after: Jacob tore his clothes, wrapped sackcloth around his waist, and mourned for his son for many days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob tore his garments and put sackcloth on his loins and mourned for his son many days.

verses.rationale: Retains the unexplained daughters, Sheol, and unresolved grief without interpreting the afterlife image.
verses.before: All his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted and said, “No, I will go down to Sheol to my son, mourning.” Thus his father wept for him.
verses.after: All his sons and daughters came to comfort him, but he refused their comfort. “No,” he said, “I will go down to my son in Sheol mourning.” And his father continued to weep for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: All his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted and said, “No, I shall go down to Sheol to my son, mourning.” Thus his father wept for him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s Midianite identification rather than harmonizing it with Ishmaelites; official is noted as a potentially broader term.
verses.before: Meanwhile the Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard.
verses.after: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh’s officials and captain of the guard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Meanwhile the Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard.

verses.rationale: Conveys the movement away from his brothers and association with Hirah naturally.
verses.before: It happened at that time that Judah went down from his brothers and turned aside to a certain Adullamite whose name was Hirah.
verses.after: About that time Judah left his brothers and settled near an Adullamite named Hirah.
verses.tsw_comparator: It happened at that time that Judah went down from his brothers and turned aside to a certain Adullamite whose name was Hirah.

verses.rationale: Prevents the common error of naming Judah’s unnamed wife Shua and states the sexual idiom plainly.
verses.before: There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite whose name was Shua. He took her and went in to her.
verses.after: There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua. He married her and slept with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite whose name was Shua. He took her and went in to her.

verses.rationale: Identifies Judah as the masculine naming subject preserved by the source.
verses.before: And she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
verses.after: She became pregnant and gave birth to a son, and Judah named him Er.
verses.tsw_comparator: And she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.

verses.rationale: Preserves the change to the mother as naming subject.
verses.before: She conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
verses.after: She became pregnant again and gave birth to a son, and she named him Onan.
verses.tsw_comparator: She conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.

verses.rationale: Retains the third birth and the location clause without making it causal.
verses.before: Yet again she bore a son, and she called his name Shelah. Judah was at Chezib when she bore him.
verses.after: She gave birth to another son and named him Shelah. Judah was in Chezib when she gave birth to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet again she bore a son, and she called his name Shelah. Judah was at Chezib when she bore him.

verses.rationale: Uses natural English while preserving Judah’s initiative, Tamar’s name, and Er’s status.
verses.before: Then Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
verses.after: Judah chose a wife named Tamar for Er, his firstborn son.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator’s terse assessment without inventing the offense.
verses.before: Yet Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD put him to death.
verses.after: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, so the LORD put him to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD put him to death.

verses.rationale: Names Tamar’s widowhood and explains the kinship duty without implying ordinary marriage consent.
verses.before: Then Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her and raise up offspring for your brother.”
verses.after: Then Judah told Onan, “Sleep with your brother’s widow. Fulfill your duty as her brother-in-law and provide offspring for your brother.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her and raise up offspring for your brother.”

verses.rationale: States the repeated sexual exploitation and deliberate refusal of family duty without euphemism or misidentifying the offense.
verses.before: Yet Onan knew that the offspring would not be his. So whenever he went in to his brother’s wife, he wasted his seed on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
verses.after: Onan knew that the offspring would not be counted as his. So whenever he slept with his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground to keep from providing offspring for his brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Onan knew that the offspring would not be his. So whenever he went in to his brother’s wife, he wasted his seed on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.

verses.rationale: Connects the judgment specifically to Onan’s described conduct.
verses.before: What he did was evil in the sight of the LORD, and he put him to death also.
verses.after: What he did was evil in the LORD’s sight, so the LORD put him to death as well.
verses.tsw_comparator: What he did was evil in the sight of the LORD, and he put him to death also.

verses.rationale: Separates Judah’s stated promise from his concealed fear and preserves Tamar’s constrained position.
verses.before: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father’s house until Shelah my son grows up.” For he feared that he also might die, like his brothers. So Tamar went and remained in her father’s house.
verses.after: Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, “Remain a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up.” He was thinking, “He might die too, like his brothers.” So Tamar went and lived in her father’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father’s house until Shelah my son grows up.” For he feared that he also might die, like his brothers. So Tamar went and remained in her father’s house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wife unnamed, preserves mourning, and identifies the destination and companion.
verses.before: After many days the daughter of Shua, Judah’s wife, died. When Judah was comforted, he went up to Timnah to his sheep shearers, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
verses.after: A long time passed, and Judah’s wife—the daughter of Shua—died. After Judah’s mourning ended, he went up to his sheep shearers at Timnah with his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
verses.tsw_comparator: After many days the daughter of Shua, Judah’s wife, died. When Judah was comforted, he went up to Timnah to his sheep shearers, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.

verses.rationale: Retains the report and kinship relationship directly.
verses.before: Tamar was told, “Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”
verses.after: Tamar was told, “Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Tamar was told, “Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Tamar’s deliberate response to Judah’s broken obligation without moralizing it.
verses.before: So she removed her widow’s garments and covered herself with a veil, wrapping herself up, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that Shelah had grown up, yet she had not been given to him as a wife.
verses.after: She took off her widow’s clothes, covered herself with a veil, and wrapped herself up. Then she sat at the entrance to Enaim on the road to Timnah, because she saw that Shelah had grown up but she had not been given to him as a wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she removed her widow’s garments and covered herself with a veil, wrapping herself up, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that Shelah had grown up, yet she had not been given to him as a wife.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah’s mistaken inference distinct from the narrator’s description.
verses.before: When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.
verses.after: When Judah saw her, he assumed she was a prostitute because she had covered her face.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

verses.rationale: States the proposed transaction clearly while preserving Judah’s ignorance.
verses.before: He turned aside to her by the roadside and said, “Come, let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. She said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”
verses.after: Not realizing she was his daughter-in-law, he turned toward her beside the road and said, “Come, let me sleep with you.” She asked, “What will you give me to sleep with you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned aside to her by the roadside and said, “Come, let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. She said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”

verses.rationale: Makes the delayed payment and security request explicit.
verses.before: He answered, “I will send a young goat from the flock.” And she said, “Will you give me a pledge until you send it?”
verses.after: “I’ll send you a young goat from my flock,” he answered. She said, “Will you give me something as a pledge until you send it?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He answered, “I will send a young goat from the flock.” And she said, “Will you give me a pledge until you send it?”

verses.rationale: Retains the three identifying objects and conception without embellishment.
verses.before: He said, “What pledge will I give you?” She answered, “Your seal and your cord and the staff that is in your hand.” So he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
verses.after: “What pledge should I give you?” he asked. She answered, “Your seal, its cord, and the staff in your hand.” He gave them to her and slept with her, and she became pregnant by him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “What pledge shall I give you?” She answered, “Your seal and your cord and the staff that is in your hand.” So he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.

verses.rationale: Preserves Tamar’s restoration of her public identity.
verses.before: Then she arose and went away, and removing her veil, she put on the garments of her widowhood.
verses.after: Then she got up and left. She removed her veil and put her widow’s clothes back on.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she arose and went away, and removing her veil, she put on the garments of her widowhood.

verses.rationale: Names Hirah for clarity and preserves the failed exchange.
verses.before: When Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend the Adullamite to recover the pledge from the woman, he did not find her.
verses.after: Judah sent the young goat with his Adullamite friend to retrieve the pledge from the woman, but Hirah could not find her.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend the Adullamite to recover the pledge from the woman, he did not find her.

verses.rationale: Renders qedeshah distinctly while leaving its precise institutional meaning to a note.

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete reversal and awakening.
verses.before: And the ugly and thin cows ate up the seven attractive and fat cows. Then Pharaoh awoke.
verses.after: The ugly, gaunt cows ate the seven healthy, well-fed cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the ugly and thin cows ate up the seven attractive and fat cows. Then Pharaoh awoke.

verses.rationale: Uses heads of grain for the agricultural term and keeps number, quality, and one stalk.
verses.before: And he fell asleep and dreamed a second time. And look, seven ears of grain, plump and good, were growing on one stalk.
verses.after: He fell asleep and dreamed a second time. Seven full, healthy heads of grain were growing on one stalk.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he fell asleep and dreamed a second time. And behold, seven ears of grain, plump and good, were growing on one stalk.

verses.rationale: Preserves number, sequence, and destructive wind.
verses.before: And look, seven ears, thin and scorched by the east wind, sprang up after them.
verses.after: Then seven thin heads of grain, scorched by the east wind, sprouted behind them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, seven ears, thin and scorched by the east wind, sprang up after them.

verses.rationale: Renders the final behold as recognition while retaining swallowing imagery.
verses.before: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven plump and full ears. Then Pharaoh awoke, and look, it was a dream.
verses.after: The thin heads swallowed the seven full, healthy heads. Pharaoh woke up and realized it was a dream.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven plump and full ears. Then Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

verses.rationale: Keeps inner disturbance, both expert groups, plural dreams, and their failure.
verses.before: In the morning his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.
verses.after: In the morning Pharaoh’s spirit was disturbed. He summoned all Egypt’s magicians and wise men and told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the morning his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.

verses.rationale: Allows the plural to include his past offense and his failure to remember Joseph.
verses.before: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my offenses today.
verses.after: Then the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, “Today I am reminded of my offenses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my offenses today.

verses.rationale: Naturalizes the cupbearer’s retelling while preserving location and companion.
verses.before: Pharaoh was angry with his servants and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker.
verses.after: Pharaoh was angry with his servants and placed the chief baker and me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh was angry with his servants and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker.

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic pairing and distinct interpretations.
verses.before: We dreamed a dream on the same night, he and I, each dream with its own meaning.
verses.after: He and I each had a dream on the same night, and each dream had its own meaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: We dreamed a dream on the same night, he and I, each dream with its own meaning.

verses.rationale: Preserves Joseph’s youth, ethnicity, enslaved status, and individualized interpretations.
verses.before: A young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him, and he interpreted our dreams to us, giving each man an interpretation according to his dream.
verses.after: A young Hebrew man was there with us, a slave belonging to the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he interpreted each one according to its meaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: A young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him, and he interpreted our dreams to us, giving each man an interpretation according to his dream.

verses.rationale: Names Pharaoh as the actions’ implicit subject and retains both outcomes.
verses.before: And just as he interpreted to us, so it happened. I was restored to my office, and the baker was hanged.”
verses.after: Everything happened exactly as he interpreted: Pharaoh restored me to my position and hanged the baker.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And just as he interpreted to us, so it came to pass. I was restored to my office, and the baker was hanged.”

verses.rationale: Keeps prison-as-pit continuity and all preparations without assuming whether he shaved hair or beard.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they quickly brought him out of the pit. And when he had shaved himself and changed his garments, he came before Pharaoh.
verses.after: Pharaoh sent for Joseph, and they hurried him out of the pit. Joseph shaved, changed his clothes, and came before Pharaoh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they quickly brought him out of the pit. And when he had shaved himself and changed his garments, he came before Pharaoh.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pharaoh’s claim about Joseph’s ability and the repetition of interpretation.
verses.before: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
verses.after: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I had a dream, but no one can interpret it. I have heard that when you hear a dream, you can interpret it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Joseph’s self-denial and the consequential, somewhat ambiguous shalom wording rather than reducing it to favorable.
verses.before: Joseph answered Pharaoh, “It is not in me. God will give Pharaoh a favorable answer.”
verses.after: Joseph answered Pharaoh, “The answer is not in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joseph answered Pharaoh, “It is not in me. God will give Pharaoh a favorable answer.”

verses.rationale: Begins Pharaoh’s retelling in direct, natural syntax.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream, look, I was standing on the bank of the Nile.
verses.after: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I was standing on the bank of the Nile.

verses.rationale: Retains number, source, qualities, and grazing place.
verses.before: And look, seven cows, fat and attractive, came up out of the Nile and grazed among the reeds.
verses.after: Suddenly seven well-fed, fine-looking cows came up from the Nile and grazed among the reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, seven cows, fat and attractive, came up out of the Nile and grazed among the reeds.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pharaoh’s intensified additions in the retelling.
verses.before: And look, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I had never seen in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
verses.after: Then seven other cows came up behind them—weak, terribly ugly, and gaunt. I had never seen such ugly cows anywhere in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I had never seen in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the action and contrast concisely.
verses.before: And the thin and ugly cows ate up the first seven fat cows,
verses.after: The gaunt, ugly cows ate the first seven well-fed cows.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the thin and ugly cows ate up the first seven fat cows,

verses.rationale: Preserves the dream’s unnatural detail and Pharaoh’s awakening.
verses.before: but when they had eaten them, no one would have known that they had eaten them, for they were still as ugly as before. Then I awoke.
verses.after: But even after swallowing them, no one could tell they had done so. They looked as ugly as before. Then I woke up.
verses.tsw_comparator: but when they had eaten them, no one would have known that they had eaten them, for they were still as ugly as before. Then I awoke.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the shift to the second dream while retaining its elements and continuing Pharaoh’s speech.
verses.before: I also saw in my dream seven ears growing on one stalk, full and good.
verses.after: In my next dream I saw seven full, healthy heads of grain growing on one stalk.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also saw in my dream seven ears growing on one stalk, full and good.

verses.rationale: Keeps the added withered descriptor in Pharaoh’s retelling.
verses.before: And look, seven ears, withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind, sprang up after them.
verses.after: Then seven withered, thin heads, scorched by the east wind, sprouted behind them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind, sprang up after them.

verses.rationale: Preserves swallowing and the experts’ inability.
verses.before: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven good ears. And I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”
verses.after: The thin heads swallowed the seven healthy heads. I told the magicians, but none of them could explain it to me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven good ears. And I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”

verses.rationale: Makes the referent plural while retaining the assertion of one message and divine disclosure.
verses.before: Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one. God has revealed to Pharaoh what he is about to do.
verses.after: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh’s two dreams are one. God has told Pharaoh what he is about to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one. God has revealed to Pharaoh what he is about to do.

verses.rationale: Keeps both numerical equations and their unity.
verses.before: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years. The dreams are one.
verses.after: The seven healthy cows are seven years, and the seven healthy heads of grain are seven years. It is one dream.
verses.tsw_comparator: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years. The dreams are one.

verses.rationale: Retains every symbolic correspondence and future famine.
verses.before: The seven thin and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears scorched by the east wind are seven years of famine.
verses.after: The seven gaunt, ugly cows that came up behind them are seven years, and the seven empty heads scorched by the east wind will be seven years of famine.
verses.tsw_comparator: The seven thin and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears scorched by the east wind are seven years of famine.

verses.rationale: Preserves repetition that confirms the interpretation.
verses.before: It is as I told Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
verses.after: It is just as I told Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is as I told Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.

verses.rationale: Uses immediate future language while retaining extent and magnitude.
verses.before: Look, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Seven years of great abundance are about to come throughout Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast, forgetting, and consuming image.
verses.before: But after them seven years of famine will arise, and all the abundance will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land.
verses.after: After them, seven years of famine will arise. All Egypt’s abundance will be forgotten, and the famine will consume the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: But after them seven years of famine will arise, and all the abundance will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land.

verses.rationale: Expresses the not-known idiom clearly while preserving cause and intensity.
verses.before: The abundance will not be known in the land because of the famine that follows, for it will be very severe.
verses.after: No trace of the former abundance will remain in the land because the famine that follows will be so severe.
verses.tsw_comparator: The abundance will not be known in the land because of the famine that follows, for it will be very severe.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine certainty and urgency without implying two unrelated dreams.
verses.before: And the doubling of Pharaoh’s dream means that the matter is established by God, and God will soon bring it about.
verses.after: The dream was repeated to Pharaoh because God has firmly established the matter, and God will soon bring it about.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the doubling of Pharaoh’s dream means that the matter is established by God, and God will soon bring it about.

verses.rationale: Retains both qualifications and national authority while continuing Joseph’s speech.
verses.before: Now therefore let Pharaoh select a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.
verses.after: So now Pharaoh should look for a discerning and wise man and put him in charge of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore let Pharaoh select a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Chooses the contextual taxation sense of the rare verb and preserves the precise fraction.
verses.before: Let Pharaoh proceed to appoint overseers over the land and take one-fifth of the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
verses.after: Pharaoh should appoint overseers throughout the land and collect one-fifth of Egypt’s produce during the seven years of abundance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let Pharaoh proceed to appoint overseers over the land and take one-fifth of the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.

verses.rationale: Retains gathering, royal control, urban storage, and guarding.
verses.before: Let them gather all the food of these coming good years and store up grain under Pharaoh’s authority for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
verses.after: They should gather food during the good years ahead and store grain under Pharaoh’s authority as food in the cities, keeping it secure.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them gather all the food of these coming good years and store up grain under Pharaoh’s authority for food in the cities, and let them keep it.

verses.rationale: Uses reserve and preserves the life-saving purpose.
verses.before: That food will be a reserve for the land against the seven years of famine that will occur in the land of Egypt, so that the land may not perish through the famine.”
verses.after: The food will be a reserve for Egypt during the seven years of famine, so the land will not be destroyed by the famine.”
verses.tsw_comparator: That food shall be a reserve for the land against the seven years of famine that will occur in the land of Egypt, so that the land may not perish through the famine.”

verses.rationale: Existing wording is concise and accurate.
verses.before: The proposal seemed good to Pharaoh and to all his servants.
verses.after: The proposal seemed good to Pharaoh and all his servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The proposal seemed good to Pharaoh and to all his servants.

verses.rationale: Leaves spirit of God’s capitalization interpretively open in Pharaoh’s polytheistic setting.
verses.before: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find a man like this, in whom is the Spirit of God?”
verses.after: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Could we find anyone like this man, in whom is the spirit of God?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find a man like this, in whom is the Spirit of God?”

verses.rationale: Preserves Pharaoh’s reasoning and both wisdom terms.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is none so discerning and wise as you.
verses.after: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has revealed all this to you, no one is as discerning and wise as you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is none so discerning and wise as you.

verses.rationale: Uses obey as the contextual sense of the uncertain mouth-related expression while retaining Pharaoh’s sole superiority.
verses.before: You will be over my house, and all my people will order themselves according to your command. Only with respect to the throne will I be greater than you.”
verses.after: You will be over my household, and all my people will obey your command. Only with regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall be over my house, and all my people shall order themselves according to your command. Only with respect to the throne will I be greater than you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the formal appointment and territorial scope.
verses.before: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
verses.after: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “See, I have placed you over all the land of Egypt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all three public symbols of delegated status.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh took his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph’s hand and clothed him in garments of fine linen and put a gold chain around his neck.
verses.after: Pharaoh removed his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph’s hand. He dressed Joseph in fine linen and placed a gold chain around his neck.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh took his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph’s hand and clothed him in garments of fine linen and put a gold chain around his neck.

verses.rationale: Uses a cautious functional rendering of the uncertain Egyptian/Hebrew acclamation and notes the ambiguity.
verses.before: And he had him ride in his second chariot. And they cried out before him, “Bow the knee!” Thus he set him over all the land of Egypt.
verses.after: He had Joseph ride in his second chariot while people called out before him, “Make way!” In this way Pharaoh placed him over all Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he had him ride in his second chariot. And they cried out before him, “Bow the knee!” Thus he set him over all the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Makes the idiom one of effective authority while retaining Pharaoh’s title.
verses.before: Moreover Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, and without your permission no one will lift hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.”
verses.after: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your authorization no one will lift a hand or foot anywhere in Egypt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, and without your permission no one shall lift hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the Egyptian names, marriage arranged by Pharaoh, priesthood, and Joseph’s new reach without guessing name meanings.
verses.before: Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-paneah. And he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as a wife. So Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah and gave him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera the priest of On, as his wife. Then Joseph went out through the land of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-paneah. And he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as a wife. So Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact age, royal service, and nationwide journey.
verses.before: Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from Pharaoh’s presence and traveled through all the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. He left Pharaoh’s presence and traveled throughout Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from Pharaoh’s presence and traveled through all the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual handfuls expression while supplying its agricultural object from context.
verses.before: During the seven years of abundance the earth produced plentifully.
verses.after: During the seven years of abundance, the land produced crops by the handfuls.
verses.tsw_comparator: During the seven years of abundance the earth produced plentifully.

verses.rationale: Clarifies Joseph’s subject and preserves local storage practice.
verses.before: And he gathered all the food of those seven years that occurred in the land of Egypt and stored up food in the cities. In each city he stored up food from the fields surrounding it.
verses.after: Joseph gathered all the food produced in Egypt during those seven years and stored it in the cities. In each city he stored the food grown in its surrounding fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he gathered all the food of those seven years that occurred in the land of Egypt and stored up food in the cities. In each city he stored up food from the fields surrounding it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ancestral sand image and repeated measure/count language.
verses.before: Joseph stored up grain like the sand of the sea, exceedingly much, until he ceased measuring it, for it could not be measured.
verses.after: Joseph stored up grain in enormous quantities, like the sand of the sea, until he stopped measuring it because it was beyond measure.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joseph stored up grain like the sand of the sea, exceedingly much, until he ceased measuring it, for it could not be measured.

verses.rationale: Preserves timing, number, maternity, and Asenath’s lineage.
verses.before: Before the years of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph, whom Asenath the daughter of Potiphera priest of On bore to him.
verses.after: Before the famine years began, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath, daughter of Potiphera the priest of On.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before the years of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph, whom Asenath the daughter of Potiphera priest of On bore to him.

verses.rationale: Retains the name association and Joseph’s difficult claim without implying literal amnesia.
verses.before: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father’s house.”
verses.after: Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, saying, “God has made me forget all my hardship and my whole father’s household.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father’s house.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the name association and holds fruitfulness together with affliction.
verses.before: And the name of the second he called Ephraim, “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
verses.after: He named the second son Ephraim, saying, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my suffering.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the name of the second he called Ephraim, “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”

verses.rationale: Continues the sentence while retaining number, condition, and place.
verses.before: Then the seven years of abundance that had occurred in the land of Egypt came to an end,
verses.after: The seven years of abundance in Egypt came to an end,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the seven years of abundance that had occurred in the land of Egypt came to an end,

verses.rationale: Uses food for bread’s broader contextual sense and preserves worldwide/Egypt contrast.
verses.before: and the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
verses.after: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. Famine struck every land, but throughout Egypt there was food.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

verses.rationale: Preserves public distress, appeal, and Joseph’s delegated authority.
verses.before: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
verses.after: When all Egypt began to feel the famine, the people cried to Pharaoh for food. Pharaoh told all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”

verses.rationale: Retains the ancient face image and the sale—not free distribution—while supplying storehouses from context.
verses.before: So when the famine had spread over all the face of the earth, Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians, for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: The famine covered the whole face of the land. Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians as the famine grew severe in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: So when the famine had spread over all the face of the earth, Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians, for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Expresses the universal idiom naturally while preserving destination, transaction, and cause.
verses.before: And all the earth came to Egypt to Joseph to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.
verses.after: People from every land came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph because the famine was severe throughout the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all the earth came to Egypt to Joseph to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.
